 After winning the T20I series 3-2, India will enter the five-match ODI series looking to improve their 50-over record in New Zealand – read on for how to watch New Zealand vs India live, including teams, news, and where to find a free stream.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Both teams have named split squads, rotating players to keep them fresh for the two-match Test series that follows. Shubman Gill will captain India for the first three ODIs, while Shreyas Iyer will take over for the final two. Mitchell Santner will lead New Zealand throughout the five-match series.
 The Kiwis will be without Devon Conway for the opening ODI after he suffered a concussion in a collision with Matt Henry during a training session. Henry himself is uncertain to feature, while Tim Seifert has been brought in to replace Conway. Tom Latham, Daryl Mitchell, and the in-form Glenn Phillips will need to hold the fort with the bat, while Jacob Duffy, Kyle Jamieson, and Will Young will be their main bowling options.
 The biggest talking point for India, once again, is the return of Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma, both legends who now play only the ODI format. They're both in fine nick, having registered a century each in the recently concluded series against the West Indies. India's bowling, however, remains a concern. Can the likes of Mohammed Siraj, Arshdeep Singh, and Kuldeep Yadav deliver?
 The opening match will be played at Eden Park in Auckland, a ground known for its unusual dimensions and short straight boundaries of just 50-55 meters. That could make it tempting for batters to go big, although the conditions could become particularly interesting under lights, when the new ball may offer more swing, bounce and seam movement.

 What is India's ODI record against New Zealand?
 Of the 45 matches played between the two sides so far, India have won only 14 and lost 26. Their last ODI win in New Zealand came way back in February 2019. India also lost the last ODI series against the Kiwis 2-1, played at home in January 2026.
